problem: The sentence defines mAP as averaging precision-recall scores over IoU thresholds only. In standard textbooks, average precision (AP) is the area under the precision-recall curve for one class at one IoU threshold, and mAP is the mean of AP over classes (COCO also averages over IoU thresholds). As written, a student would think the averaging is only over thresholds.
fix: For each class, compute AP as the area under its precision-recall curve at a fixed IoU threshold; mAP is the mean of AP over all classes, and benchmark suites such as COCO additionally average over IoU thresholds from 0.5 to 0.95.

problem: NMS is described as sorting all boxes by score together. In a multi-class detector, boxes of different classes must not suppress each other, so NMS is run separately for each class.
fix: Add: NMS is applied per class — boxes are grouped by predicted class, and suppression with the IoU threshold happens within each class group.
